# awacino_beamin_device (Resource)

An unattended server as a Beam-in device of the company. Creating the resource makes a **one-time setup code** (an enrolment) with ready install lines (`install_docker`, `install_apt`, `cloud_init`). Put `cloud_init` into the server's user data (or run one of the install lines); the server installs the Awacino client, connects outbound only and registers as a Beam-in device within minutes. With `wait_for_device = true` the apply waits for that and `device_id` is known afterwards.

Destroying the resource removes the registered device from the company, or revokes the setup code while it is unused. A device beyond the plan's Beam-in limit waits in the Lobby (`status = "lobby"`).

Needs the key section **Connections** (Write).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A one-time setup code for a new server, with ready install lines.
resource "awacino_beamin_device" "web01" {
  label       = "web-01.example.net"
  external_id = "cust4711-web01"
  hours       = 2
}

# Put the setup code into the server's user data - here Hetzner Cloud as an example:
# resource "hcloud_server" "web01" {
#   name        = "web-01"
#   server_type = "cx22"
#   image       = "debian-12"
#   user_data   = awacino_beamin_device.web01.cloud_init
# }

# The registered device, in the same apply: the data source waits until the server has registered.
# (Do not set wait_for_device on web01 here - the server is only created after web01 is done.)
# data "awacino_device" "web01" {
#   external_id  = awacino_beamin_device.web01.external_id
#   wait_timeout = "15m"
#   depends_on   = [hcloud_server.web01]
# }

# A server that is set up outside this configuration: wait in the resource itself.
resource "awacino_beamin_device" "db01" {
  label           = "db-01.example.net"
  wait_for_device = true
  wait_timeout    = "30m"
}

output "db01_install" {
  value     = awacino_beamin_device.db01.install_apt
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) Name of the new device (1-64 characters, unique among the company's devices), for example its host name.

### Optional

- `external_id` (String) Your own id for the server (up to 128 characters); the `awacino_devices` data source filters by it.
- `hours` (Number) Hours the setup code pairs (1-24, default 2). An unused code that ran out never pairs.
- `name` (String) The device's name once it registered (starts as `label`). Set it to rename the device.
- `wait_for_device` (Boolean) Wait in apply until the server has registered (polls with back-off 2 to 30 s). Default `false`.
- `wait_timeout` (String) How long `wait_for_device` waits (Go duration, default `15m`).

### Read-Only

- `cloud_init` (String, Sensitive) A `#cloud-config` document with the setup code, for the server's `user_data`.
- `device_id` (String) The registered device's id - known once the server registered (use `wait_for_device`).
- `enrolment_state` (String) `open`, `used` (the server registered), `expired` or `revoked`.
- `expires_at` (String) When the setup code stops pairing.
- `id` (String) Enrolment id (`enr_...`); the device id when the resource was imported by device id.
- `install_apt` (String, Sensitive) Shell lines for Debian / Ubuntu with the setup code.
- `install_docker` (String, Sensitive) A `docker run` line with the setup code.
- `platform` (String) Platform the device reported (`linux`, `docker`, ...).
- `setup_code` (String, Sensitive) The one-time setup code (Docker `AWACINO_SETUP_CODE`). Known only on create.
- `status` (String) `active` or `lobby` once registered; `pending` before.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By enrolment id (a setup code made by the API) ...
terraform import awacino_beamin_device.web01 enr_81c416950b1be7e3

# ... or by the id of an existing Beam-in device
terraform import awacino_beamin_device.web01 2f0c3c1e-8a4b-4d1e-9a51-1f3b2a7c9d10
```
